title: Two particles on a line: direction and speed

stimulus.title: Positions of two particles
stimulus.html:
Particles PP and QQ move along the xx-axis for 0≤t≤60 \le t \le 6. Their positions are given below, with xx in meters and tt in seconds.
Positions of particles P and Q at time t seconds, in meters
ParticlePosition
PPxP(t)x_P(t)=2t3−15t2+24t+5= 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 24t + 5
QQxQ(t)=(t−2)e−t/2x_Q(t) = (t - 2)e^{-t/2}

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the velocity of particle PP at time t=2t = 2. Is PP moving to the left or to the right at t=2t = 2? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(t) = 6t^2 - 30t + 24</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(2) = -12</annotation></semantics></math> meters per second
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 24 - 60 + 24</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -12</annotation></semantics></math>
the reason must be the sign of the velocity

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x_P'(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6t^2 - 30t + 24</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 24 - 60 + 24</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -12</annotation></semantics></math> meters per second. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(2) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, particle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> is moving to the left at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is particle PP speeding up or slowing down at time t=2t = 2? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_P(t) = 12t - 30</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_P(2) = -6</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_P(2) = 24 - 30 = -6</annotation></semantics></math> meters per second per second

rubric.point: Speeding up, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_P(2)</annotation></semantics></math> are both negative
accept: both signs must be named; "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a < 0</annotation></semantics></math>" alone does not earn the point

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_P(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= v_P'(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 12t - 30</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_P(2) = -6</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(2) = -12 < 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_P(2) = -6 < 0</annotation></semantics></math> have the same sign, particle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> is speeding up at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find all times tt, for 0<t<60 < t < 6, at which particle PP changes direction. Justify your answer.

rubric.point: Solves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(t) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6(t - 1)(t - 4) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: factoring <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6t^2 - 30t + 24</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6(t^2 - 5t + 4)</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> changes direction at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math> because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P</annotation></semantics></math> changes sign at each
accept: from positive to negative at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, from negative to positive at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>

"<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P = 0</annotation></semantics></math>" without the sign change does not earn the point

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(t) = 6(t - 1)(t - 4)</annotation></semantics></math> is 0 at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>. It changes from positive to negative at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and from negative to positive at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, so particle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> changes direction at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the velocity vQ(t)v_Q(t) of particle QQ. At time t=3t = 3, are particles PP and QQ moving in the same direction? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= e^{-t/2} - \frac{t - 2}{2}e^{-t/2}</annotation></semantics></math>, by the product and chain rules
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{4 - t}{2}e^{-t/2}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}e^{-3/2} > 0</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= e^{-3/2} - \frac{1}{2}e^{-3/2}</annotation></semantics></math>

the sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(3)</annotation></semantics></math> with supporting work

rubric.point: Not the same direction: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(3) = -12 < 0</annotation></semantics></math> while <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(3) > 0</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> moves left and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> moves right at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: By the product rule and the chain rule, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1 \cdot e^{-t/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ (t - 2) \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}e^{-t/2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{4 - t}{2}e^{-t/2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_Q(3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}e^{-3/2} > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> moves right. Also <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_P(3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6(2)(-1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -12 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> moves left. They are moving in opposite directions at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
